messages.subject: Looking for mentors.
messages.body_plain:
I wish to write bindings for ChainerX <https://chainer.org/> (deep learning framework) in R using RCpp.
Having worked with both R and chainerx for a while, I think this would be a great addition to the R as well as chainer framework
and extremely beneficial for the data scientists.
I have studied the RStudio bindings for tensorflow, but it is over the Python API
making it slow because of the overhead.
What makes my project unique is that I am planning to wrap the C++ API of ChainerX, the core, directly.
Interfacing directly with the core code has a lot of advantages such as removing the middleman,
improving stability, being easier to deploy and the fact that there is lesser overhead for calling any function.

I am already involved with the members of Chainer community and I am pretty well versed with the code base.

I have also prepared a 20 page long proposal for the same and I would be extremely delighted if any mentor
would be interested to work with me and take a look at my proposal.

messages.subject: [R GSoC] Timelines and next steps for 2019 R GSoC
messages.subject_clean: [R GSoC] Timelines and next steps for 2019 R GSoC
messages.body_plain:
All,

We are getting close to significant deadlines for both mentors and
prospective students for GSoC 2019.  This email is my attempt to
provide a little bit of guidance on what interested parties need to do.

Prospective Students: (see below for mentors)

At this point, you should be working on your application drafts.
Hopefully you have been communicating with the mentors for a project
idea and completing any tests in the project idea.

You should also be registered as a student on the Summer of Code
website:

https://summerofcode.withgoogle.com/

If you have not done so, do this immediately!  You will need to provide
proof of eligibility to Google, a process which can go very smoothly,
or can take significant time.  We have at least one promising student
application almost every year which can not participate in GSoC because
the eligibility approvals don't get done in time!  So fill out
everything Google asks for, follow directions carefully, and watch for
requests for more information from Google until you are certain that
you are eligible.  Org admins (Toby and I) cannot help you with this,
so you need to be diligent about it.

Once you are registered on the Summer of Code website, the immediate
next step is to post your *draft* application.  The application should
follow R GSoC's application template:

https://github.com/rstats-gsoc/gsoc2019/wiki/application-template

Make sure that you mark your google doc so that R mentors can comment
on your draft application.  You should work to address mentor comments
and continue to improve your application until close to the application
deadline.

*Before* the final deadline on April 9, 2019 13:00 (Central Daylight
Time) 19:00 (GMT) you need to submit your final application.  Per
program rules, we can only use your final application to evaluate your
application.  Google's deadlines are firm, so give yourself at least a
little time to work out any issues.

Mentors:

Thanks to a tremendous amount of help from Vijay Barve, a former R GSoC
student and now many-year mentor, I have now invited all the mentors
for whom email addresses are available in the project idea pages to be
mentors for R GSoC 2019.

If you have not received an invitation, email Toby and me immediately
with links to your project idea page and a request to be invited to
mentor.

All mentors need to sign up on the summerofcode website.  Then you will
be able to see student draft applications.

As described above, your primary responsibility beyond signing up prior
to the April 9th submission deadline is to *communicate* with
prospective students via comments on their tests, applications, and
questions.  Please be as responsive as your schedules allow.

This will be the first of many times you will see me communicate this,
but this is a reminder that under no circumstances can you communicate
with a prospective student about their acceptance to the program.
Google makes final project slot allocations, and program rules require
that *only Google* will communicate acceptance or rejection of
applications to to prospective students.

If you have any questions or problems feel free to send them to this
list if they are non-confidential and of general utility to the other
list participants, or to me and Toby as the organization admins for R's
participation in GSoC.

Regards,

Brian

--
Brian G. Peterson
http://braverock.com/brian/

IM: bgpbraverock

messages.subject: Fwd: GSoC 2019: Final PDF review and Slot Allocation
messages.subject_clean: GSoC 2019: Final PDF review and Slot Allocation
messages.body_plain:
Updated information from google regarding the next steps, in case anyone didn't receive this from Google.  - Brian

---------- Forwarded message ---------
From: Google Summer of Code <summerofco...@google.com>
Date: Sat, Apr 6, 2019 at 3:23 PM
Subject: GSoC 2019: Final PDF review and Slot Allocation

Hi Brian Peterson,

The student submission period is nearly over - you can expect a lot of proposals coming in over these last 3 days - we're already at record numbers of students registering for GSoC! We know you are all quite busy responding to students and giving them feedback on their draft proposals. In the next phase of GSoC, you select which of these proposals you choose for GSoC projects.
Reviewing Final PDF Proposals: April

The deadline for students to submit their Final PDF proposal is Tuesday, April 9 at 18:00 UTC.
Students without Final PDF proposals cannot be accepted, and there will be no exceptions.

After April 9 at 18:00 UTC, org members will be able to see the Final PDFs submitted by students.

April 9 18:00 UTC is also the deadline for students to submit a proof of enrollment in an eligible university program. Students who fail to do this are ineligible for GSoC this year. We will be reviewing the forms and students will have a chance to resubmit if there are any problems.

Your decision about whether or not to select a student should be based on the Final PDF proposal. You will also be able to reference the draft proposal -- but should not make your decision based on it. A draft proposal is intended to be used to view the comment thread and maybe see how the student interacted with you and responded to comments, etc. Do not use it to let the student make more changes after the deadline. That is not fair to all the other applicants.
Want to Mentor?

If you are interested in being a mentor for a given proposal then you can click the purple "Want to Mentor" button to help your Org Admin know that you are interested. This is particularly helpful for the org admins when determining if they have enough mentors for their slot requests.
Slots Request - deadline Monday, April 22 18:00 UTC (Org Admin responsibility)
Org Admins will request a minimum and maximum number of project slots.
Slots should only be requested for projects where there is at least one confirmed mentor and where the student has a good chance of succeeding.
Do not accept "okay" proposals.
Do not request more slots than you have mentors for - if we grant you the slots you request and you can't use all of them you have essentially taken away these slots from other orgs that could have used them and also taken away the opportunity for that number of students to participate in GSoC 2019.
New orgs will likely only receive 1-2 slots, no matter how many they request.
Mentors should be mentoring 1 project generally. In rare cases a mentor can mentor 2 projects.

April 22nd is also the deadline for students to have any re-submitted proof of enrollment forms approved. Note that students with invalid forms will not appear in your list of student projects you can choose from starting April 24th (when slots are announced to orgs).

All Org Admins should read Slot Allocation and Project Selection <https://developers.google.com/open-source/gsoc/help/slot-allocation> for more detailed information.
Upcoming Important Dates

March 25 - April 9 18:00 UTC: Students submit their Final PDF proposals through the program website for you to give solid feedback on.
April 9 - 21:  Review all submitted student proposals with your org and consider how many you want to select and how many you can handle. Decide on the minimum/maximum number of student slots to request- do not request more than your org can handle - this could take students away from orgs who have excellent student prospects and need the slots.
April 22 18:00 UTC: Deadline to submit slot requests (Org Admins enter requests)
April 24 18:00 UTC: Slot allocations are announced by Google
April 24 - May 1 18:00 UTC: Orgs select the proposals to become student projects. At least 1 mentor must be assigned to each project before it can be selected. (Org Admins enter selections)
May 1- 5: Google Program Admins will do another review of student eligibility
May 6: Accepted GSoC 2019 students/projects are announced
May 6 - 26: Community Bonding Period
May 26: Deadline to notify Google Admins of an inactive student that you wish to be removed from the program
May 27: Coding begins
June 24-28: First evaluation period - mentors evaluate students, students evaluate mentors
July 22 - 26: Second evaluation period - mentors evaluate students, students evaluate mentors
August 19 - 26: Students wrap up their projects and submit final evaluation of their mentor
August 26 - September 2: Mentors submit final evaluations of students
September 3: Students passing GSoC 2019 are announced

If you haven't done so already, be sure to read the Roles and Responsibilities <https://developers.google.com/open-source/gsoc/help/responsibilities> to understand what is expected of you and of students during the program.

Please contact us at gsoc-s...@google.com with any questions.

Google Open Source Programs Office

This email was sent to bgpbra...@gmail.com.

You are receiving this email because of your participation in Google Summer of Code 2019.
https://summerofcode.withgoogle.com

To leave the program and stop receiving all emails, you can go to your profile <https://summerofcode.withgoogle.com/dashboard/profile/> and request deletion of your program profile.

For any questions, please contact gsoc-s...@google.com. Replies to this message go to an unmonitored mailbox.

© 2019 Google LLC, 1600 Amphitheatre Parkway, Mountain View, CA 94043, USA

--
Brian G. Peterson

messages.subject: [R GSoC] IMPORTANT: Student applications close today!
messages.subject_clean: [R GSoC] IMPORTANT: Student applications close today!
messages.body_plain:
All,

Student applications close at 13:00 Central Daylight time on April 9th,
18:00 UTC 9 April.  You should see the deadline in your local time zone
here:

https://summerofcode.withgoogle.com/

That deadline is a little over *28 hours* from the time I am sending
this email.

Google's deadlines are firm.  We have no discretion or control over
them.

Students:

You need to make any final changes to your draft proposals and submit a
final PDF version following Google's instructions.

So my recommendation is to take a few more passes *today*,*now* through
your draft application and incorporate changes from any feedback you've
received from your mentors, and doing final edits.

If there is feedback you urgently desire from the mentors for your
project idea, email them.  Feel free to copy me on your email, and I
will take a look as well.

If you miss the final submission deadline, there is nothing we can do
to help you, so don't miss the deadline.

Mentors:

Your work will get even busier after the final application deadline.

For now, mentors should have two priorities:

The first is communicating with interested students and helping
(mentoring) them to improve their applications into the final
submission.

Second, all mentors that we know about have received invitations to
sign up as mentors for R GSoC on the Google Summer of Code website. You
need to take that application and finish signup ASAP.  this is the only
place you can see and comment on official student submissions.  If you
don't have an invitation, please email me and Toby as soon as you can.

As always, mentors or students with questions should reach out for
assistance.

Thanks, and good luck,

Brian

--

messages.subject: [R GSoC] Student Applications are finalized: Next Steps
messages.subject_clean: [R GSoC] Student Applications are finalized: Next Steps
messages.body_plain:
All,

Thank you for a really great crop of potential student applications.
The final applications we received ahead of the deadline are really
outstanding.

Students:

I know you want to know *right now*, but project slot awards won't be
announced until May 6th.  Please don't ask us whether you'll be
accepted, or what your chances of acceptance are, because program rules
prohibit us from telling you.  Google grants slots to the organization,
and we will allocate those slots.  Google reserves for itself the
notification of acceptance, rejection, and then pass/fail on each
evaluation.

Some of the students on this list may still have paperwork to finalize
with Google.  If you have any steps that are still provisional, watch
the summerofcode website and your email very carefully, and follow up
with the Google systems as soon as you can.  Many years, we lose
another promising student or two to trailing paperwork.  Please be
diligent about deadlines. Google's deadlines are firm.

Mentors:

This is one of the busiest times for the R GSoC mentor community.  Now
we need every one of our mentors to start evaluating the proposals
we've received.  We encourage you to comment on any proposal where you
feel you have some expertise.  The comments made on the summerofcode
website are only visible to the R mentor community.  They are not
visible to the students.  Please add your comments only there, and *do
not* discuss student proposals in any open forum (like this list). If
there is something sensitive you want to discuss, please bring it up in
an email to me and to Toby, and we will work with you on it.

Many of our project ideas have received multiple proposals.  For your
project ideas with multiple proposals, we need you to voice an opinion
on the ranking of those proposals.  Not just the first choice, but
second choice and reject recommendations as well.  Students can and do
apply to multiple projects, and not only R.  We need to know how to
value them in a competing priority world.

For project ideas that you will be a mentor for, please select 'Want to
Mentor' on the project page.  For us to slot a project, all listed
mentors must select 'Want to Mentor' and comment on the proposal (we
need clear engagement from our mentors as well!).

You may see stars show up and disappear on the proposals.  None of
these things are final yet, we are just using them to keep track of how
many slots we should request from Google.

Slot *requests* are due to Google April 22nd.  We will not request a
slot for a project proposal that is not commented on by all of the
project mentors.

If you need additional mentors added to the system, or have questions
for me and Toby, please email us as soon as possible.

As always, if potential students or mentors have questions or issues,
you know where to find us.

Regards,

Brian

--
Brian G. Peterson
http://braverock.com/brian/
Ph: 773-459-4973
IM: bgpbraverock

messages.subject: [R GSoC] Reviewing final applications
messages.body_plain:
Students:

Hold on, we're going through this as diligently as Google program rules
allow!

Mentors:

This week is a very busy time for the R GSoC mentor community.

As I write this, we have precisely one week left to request slots from
Google.

That doesn't mean that you can emulate your students and wait till the
last minute!

Toby and I need your input on these projects to decide how many slots
to request from Google.  Unlike prior years, 'extra' slots will not be
re-allocated to other organizations this year.  So we need to do our
best to request the 'correct' number of slots.

I've spent more than six hours today going through student
applications, in many cases for the third time or more.  I am adjusting
our preliminary slot requests as I continue reading and commenting.

Toby and I need all our mentors to use the application comments section
on the summerofcode site to comment on as many proposals as you feel
you are qualified to render an opinion on.  We value this input, and I
hope that the mentors of the proposals you comment on will value it as
well in terms of questions, cautions, and scope adjustment.  No
proposal is perfect, and our goals should all be especially aligned on
helping strong proposals get slots, and then become successful GSoC
projects.  I want to especially thank those of you who have taken the
time to provide feedback on proposals for other mentors ideas.

If one of your project ideas got an application, we need *all* listed
mentors to select 'Want to Mentor' and comment on the proposal.  We
*will not* request a slot for, or award a slot to, a project that does
not demonstrate mentor engagement at this early stage.

If your project ideas got more than one final student proposal, as many
did, then we need you and your co-mentors to *rank* all of the
proposals for your project idea, and make note of this in the comments
for all of the applications for this idea.  We will use this
information to slot students once we have slots from Google, and to
deal with student de-duplication if required.

Please don't leave this work to the last minute. Google and Toby and I
rely on this information to calibrate slot requests. The more
information we have, and the sooner we have it, the more smoothly this
process will go next week once we request slots.

Once Google awards slots to organizations on May 1, we need to move
quickly to assign slots to avoid potential de-duplication issues, so I
prefer to have all the information on our preferences in writing and
accounted for when we make the slot requests.

Also, as a reminder, mentors *may not* discuss selection or rejection
of student proposals with potential students.  Students, please don't
ask.  Mentors, you may not discuss this with students. Google reserves
all communication to students about acceptance, rejection, or pass/fail
to itself.

As always, please do not hesitate to reach out to Toby and me with any
questions.

Regards,

Brian

--
Brian G. Peterson

messages.subject: [GSoC R] R granted 31 slots for GSoC 2019 !
messages.subject_clean: [GSoC R] R granted 31 slots for GSoC 2019 !
messages.body_plain:
R has been granted 31 slots for this year's Google Summer of Code.

This is more slots than we have had in prior years, and shows a lot of
trust on Google's part (most organizations get one or two slots total).

We now need to be good stewards of that trust and responsibility.

Students:
Hold on, you'll know whether your proposal has been selected in two
weeks.  Please don't ask the mentors for your project idea if you';ve
been accepted, we cannot tell you.  Google reserves the right of
communication to selected or rejected students to itself.

Mentors:
Toby and I will begin the process of preliminary slot allocations to
projects.  *Nothing is Final Yet*.  We still need final de-duplication
from Google, we need to validate that we have enough mentors for
projects, and several other administrative steps.

The most important thing for mentors to remember: you *may not*
communicate with students about acceptance or rejection until *after*
the Google announcements on May 6th.

Next most important, Toby and I may need more information from you.
Especially if you had multiple applications, or have asked us for
multiple slots, we have more work to do.  We need to make sure that
there are enough mentors to cover multiple slots, and that you have a
plan for managing multiple projects (it is a lot of work).  If we ask
you for something, please get back to us as quickly as you can.
Google's deadlines are firm, and we don't have any wiggle room on
those.  Our slot allocation is final (from our side) on May 1.

If something doesn't look right on your Dashboard, or your project
applications, please contact Toby and me via private email as soon as
possible.

As always, if you have any questions, please reach out.

Regards,

Brian
